example: Use case: a password for a new email account. Settings: Password Length 16, with Uppercase, Lowercase, Numbers, and Symbols all ticked. Step 1: the tool builds a character set of 26 uppercase + 26 lowercase + 10 digits + 27 symbols = 89 characters. Step 2: it picks 16 characters at random from that set. Step 3: the strength bar reads full, because all four character types are on and the length is 16 or more. Final result: a 16-character password mixing all four character types, ready to copy. The tool does not store it, so save it in a password manager or write it down safely.

faqs.a: Longer is better. Sixteen characters with all four character types is a good default; use 20 or more for important accounts like email and banking.
faqs.q: How long should my password be?

faqs.a: The strength bar is based on which character types are ticked and whether the length is 16 or more. It is a rough guide, not a guarantee of safety.
faqs.q: What does the strength bar mean?

faqs.a: No. The password is generated in your browser and shown on screen only. It is not saved anywhere by the tool, so copy it before leaving the page.
faqs.q: Does the tool save my password?

formula: Method: the tool builds a character pool from the ticked options — Uppercase A–Z (26), Lowercase a–z (26), Numbers 0–9 (10), Symbols !@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>? (27) — then picks characters at random from the pool, one for each position, up to the chosen length (8 to 64). Strength score: one point each for mixed case, numbers, symbols, and length of 16 or more. Passwords are generated with the browser's built-in secure random generator (crypto.getRandomValues), and the result always contains at least one character from every character set you ticked.
howTo: Move the Password Length slider to your chosen length — 16 is the default.
Tick or untick Uppercase (A-Z), Lowercase (a-z), Numbers (0-9), and Symbols (!@#$) as needed.
Tap Generate to create a new password.
Check the strength bar under the password.
Tap Copy and paste the password into the account or your password manager.
intro: The Password Generator creates random passwords of a length you choose, mixing uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols, with a strength indicator.
mistakes: Using a short password of 8 characters for an important account.
Unticking symbols and numbers, which shrinks the character pool and weakens the password.
Reusing the same generated password on several sites.
Generating a password and then forgetting to copy it before closing the page — the tool does not save it.
tips: Use a different password for every important account, especially email and banking.
Sixteen characters is a good default; go longer for accounts that hold money or personal data.
Store passwords in a password manager rather than in plain notes or photos.
Turn on two-factor authentication wherever it is offered — a strong password alone is not complete protection.
No password can be called unbreakable. A long, unique password plus two-factor authentication is the practical goal.
uses: It is used to create random passwords for new accounts, replacing weak or reused passwords with a fresh one of a chosen length and character mix.
